content.text:
Use Tailwind's arbitrary-value syntax:

```html
<div id="test" className="border-[rgb(var(--foreground-rgb))]">
```

Since `--foreground-rgb` holds raw RGB components (not a full color), you need the bracket arbitrary-value form wrapping `rgb(...)`, not the `border-(--var)` CSS-variable shorthand (which expects the variable itself to be a valid color) — per src/docs/upgrade-guide.mdx "Variables in arbitrary values" (lines 711–723) and the `border-color` utility API in src/docs/border-color.mdx (lines 16–43, "Using a custom value" example, lines 278–280).
